source.title: Relative Representations Enable Portable White-Box Monitoring Across Language Models

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model behavioral compatibility using frozen probes on shared anchor-relative coordinates, rather than directly measuring pairwise representational geometry as in the claim’s original formulation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on cross-model probe transfer, scale transfer, and sensitivity to tasks and settings. Prior-work results cited in the text are not recorded as rows. Auxiliary GuardQA results measure explicitly elicited safety judgments and are not used as evidence about unelicited behavior.
record.test_reason: The study freezes a probe trained on one LLM's anchor-relative (relative-representation) coordinates and scores it on independently trained LLMs of different families and widths. This is a functional test of V4's relative-representation route to interchangeability. It also bears on V1 (a same-family 1B/8B/70B ladder and a target-accuracy correlation), V6 (sensitivity to anchors, prompt, data shift, and whether geometric scores such as CKA/RSA predict transfer) and V7 (incompleteness). It uses a different method from the originals, so T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that independently trained autoregressive LMs share substantial task-relevant relational organization, so frozen anchored probes can be reused across models, related data, scale and prompt changes. They also conclude that anchored probes resist model updates better. They frame transfer as functional evidence rather than a direct test of the Platonic hypothesis. They stress that portability is conditional: weak for low-accuracy targets and task-dependent, and it can fail even when the property is decodable in the target.
record.recipe_differences: Uses global anchor-relative angular-distance coordinates and behavioral-probe transfer, rather than directly testing the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis’s similarity geometry across modalities or model capabilities.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with task and target model, dataset direction, prompt format, anchor count in some cases, anchor aggregation, anchor mapping, probe normalization, and distance function. The paper reports that minimal prompts lower same-model trivia probes more than calibrated transfer; cosine-distance probes are less robust than angular-distance probes after updates; and related-data Guard transfer is direction-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: Anchored probes on the same model degrade less after quantization and LoRA/QLoRA refusal fine-tuning than standard probes. Angular distance is more robust than cosine.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative (anchor-based) representations are more stable than native coordinates across fine-tuning updates of the same model.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-model probes lose 8–11 AUROC under a minimal prompt, and same-model dataset transfer is direction-asymmetric.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model probe signals are sensitive to prompt and data shift even when cross-model transfer is stable.

record.problems: Probe-transfer AUROC is functional evidence about task-relevant compatibility, not a direct measurement of whole representational geometry or universal features. Results are task- and target-dependent; some results aggregate many model pairs and do not report their heterogeneity in the standard error. Some external BeaverTails estimates have few unsafe examples and high uncertainty. No shared-data/objective causal comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Did not extract every per-cell trivia external-target result, the full GuardQA appendix, local-depth sweeps, low-FPR recall tables, all anchor-count cells, or every staleness condition. These are detailed in Appendices B.3–B.9, C.2–C.9 and C.11–C.14, D.1–D.4, E, and F; retained rows prioritize primary transfer results, explicit failures, scale asymmetry, and key sensitivity findings.

untested.parts: No cross-architecture scale trend and no measure of representational geometry versus capability. Scale is tested only within the Llama 3.x family, via probe transfer.
All of V2; there are no vision or cross-modal models.
All of V3; there is no comparison of same-architecture models trained from different seeds.
All of V5; no neurons, SAE features or circuits are compared.
No systematic comparison of kNN or CKA-style convergence metrics as a function of neighbour count, and no truly out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of whether shared training data or objectives explain the alignment, and no plateau analysis.
No stitching or learned linear maps between activations.

missing.what: Target answer accuracy correlates with incoming GT transfer (Spearman 0.976, n=36). Llama-3.2-3B on TQA: 55.8% accuracy, 46.4 incoming AUROC.
Matched-profile correlation and linear CKA do not reliably predict transfer; a modest RSA association is driven by BeaverTails
Family and size groupings: exact-family pairs 84.9 vs 80.8; size buckets tied at 81.4. Source/target asymmetry, e.g. Mistral as source 66.4.
Anchor-aggregation and anchor-pool choices change joint transfer (mean-token: calibrated 72.4→75.0, naive 70.1→65.8; mixed anchors)
Pooled-MMLU anchors: 300 vs 1000 gives 76.8 vs 74.7 cross-model; GuardQA 300→600 anchors drops BeaverTails Output transfer 89.0→73.4
missing.locator: Appendix B.9 Table 25; Appendix F.4 Table 73

missing.what: Llama/Mistral Guard anchored transfer: Mistral→Llama BeaverTails only 42.9 vs 82.9 in reverse

record.verdict_notes: Probe-transfer AUROC measures functional compatibility of task-relevant directions, not whole-representation alignment. Near-ceiling tasks such as trivia Output Prediction say little about geometry. Standard errors are across seeds only and omit pair heterogeneity. Rows r21–r24 and r33–r34 are same-model results and do not bear on convergence between independent models. The record's V1 'supports' label resting on r11 alone was too strong; it is replaced here with text-based support plus a scope limit.

versions.untested_parts: The scale comparison is within one Llama family and measures probe transfer, not a general trend across architectures, objectives, data, modalities, model capability, or representational geometry.
No vision-language or other cross-modal paired image-caption alignment is tested.
Results are generally aggregated over probe seeds; the study does not compare representations or features learned from different initializations of the same architecture.
Tests frozen behavioral-probe reuse in anchor-relative coordinates, not stitching, paired-data linear activation maps, or transfer without any shared anchor examples.
No recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified or compared.

Tests selected changes to anchor count, prompt, dataset, anchor construction, and distance function; it does not comprehensively compare similarity metrics, neighbour counts, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Shows incomplete and task-dependent transfer, but does not establish a general plateau or test whether shared model training data or objectives cause the alignment.
